clue.text: Mischievous child in difficult situation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a naughty youngster, a little rascal
second meaning: a tricky predicament or mess

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster has landed in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one child in one fix; 'in' just links two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal both for a cheeky youngster and for an awkward plight, as in 'in a right mess'.

clue.text: Eyewitness parking, bishop in Sayers novel

indicators.note: novel means new or unfamiliar, so the letters before it are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness spots a parked car and a cleric in a Dorothy L. Sayers detective story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sayers novel' looks like a book title to identify, but 'novel' is the anagram signal working on the name itself plus the two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone walking past an incident is the classic chance witness to it.

clue.text: Pressure to keep two Frenchmen in business

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to pressure someone is to coerce them
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, so two of them make MM

explanation.surface: Someone is leaning on a pair of French partners in a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: M. is the French abbreviation for Monsieur, the standard crossword route to a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling activity that business means here.

clue.text: Drunk started smoking

definitions.meaning: second meaning: put a match to a cigarette

explanation.surface: A tipsy person reached for a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person's evening; 'Drunk' is an adjective, not the past tense of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for intoxicated and also describes lighting a cigarette or pipe.

clue.text: Liqueur, Italian, knocked back by a girl

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word for Italian is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A liqueur from Italy is downed in one by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking the liqueur, but it turns the abbreviation for Italian vermouth round; 'Italian' as in gin and it is a standard crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Not earning extra money from pursuit — charitable?

parts.note: a pursuit is a hobby or interest
charitable help is given free, without charge; the question mark flags the loose link

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an unpaid pastime counts as charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a loan or account that yields no extra money, i.e. no interest is charged or paid.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest-free loan or account accrues no additional payment beyond the sum itself.

clue.text: Being deciduous, they have roots

parts.note: surface reading: trees that shed their leaves each year and are anchored by roots
setter's reading: deciduous also means falling out at a certain stage, as a child's first set in the mouth does

explanation.walkthrough: Everything points to trees, but deciduous teeth is the dental term for a child's first set, and teeth have roots too.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's first teeth are shed naturally, which dentists call deciduous, and each is anchored by a root.

clue.text: Added clause about a marauder

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document or bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extra clause has been added concerning a raiding plunderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marauder is someone who makes raids in search of plunder, which is what the answer names.

clue.text: One's published yearly, the recorded events of twelve months around university

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the record word wraps the letter for university

parts.words: the recorded events of twelve months
parts.note: an annal is the record of one year's events
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A yearly publication chronicling a year at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' stands for 'one that is', so the definition is a thing published yearly, such as a children's book of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book or magazine issued once each year.

clue.text: Silk fabric matching it inside

indicators.note: inside places the word it follows within the other word

parts.note: matching things are the same
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silk material whose lining matches it.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy, rich silk cloth worn in the Middle Ages, often woven with gold thread.

clue.text: Stable one working horse

parts.note: a stall is a compartment in a stable
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means functioning, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A single working horse kept in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' reads as an adjective or the building, but it gives the stall inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, so the word is a specific kind of horse.

clue.text: Nine starting out, obstinately maintaining an attitude

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nine players refuse to start the game, stubbornly holding their position.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent describes someone who refuses to change their views or compromise.

clue.text: Look at first batsman, a revelation

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
in cricket the opener is one of the two batsmen who start the innings

explanation.surface: Watching the leading cricketer at the crease proved a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the openers are the first two batsmen in.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is something surprising that reveals a truth, which is what a revelation is.

clue.text: Greek character — he volunteers after short time

indicators.note: after tells us the words before it come second, following the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek man signs up for reserve duty after a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Retrogade move giving support to protégé going on stage

indicators.note: going on means proceeding onto, so the following piece is attached after the earlier ones

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a ward is a young person under someone's protection
a stage in a process is a step

explanation.surface: A mentor's backing of a young performer taking to the stage turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrogade' is the printed spelling of retrograde, meaning going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A backward step is a regression, a move that goes back rather than forward.

clue.text: Relaxed in NI county after injury

indicators.note: after says the county comes second, following the word for injury

parts.note: a wound is an injury
County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone recuperated in Northern Ireland after getting hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; Down is one of its six counties.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind down is to unwind and relax after effort, so wound down means relaxed.

clue.text: "Foul" — audible cry in game

parts.note: base means low, vile or foul

indicators.note: audible means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: A spectator yells 'Foul!' during a sports match.
explanation.walkthrough: A foul ball is a real baseball term, which makes the surface sit neatly in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the American bat-and-ball game, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Nozzle is not spraying, so discard

parts.note: a jet is a nozzle that emits a stream

indicators.note: spraying scatters things in all directions, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hose nozzle that will not spray should be thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away something unwanted, as cargo from a ship.

clue.text: Expression up north a serf used

indicators.note: used here means worked over or put to use, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern peasant used a regional saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase is a particular way of putting something into words, an expression.

clue.text: Stanislavsky's acting technique course?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., the system of immersive acting derived from Stanislavsky
second meaning: a procedure or way of doing something, as a course of action

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks whether the actor's technique is a course of study; 'course' is instead a separate meaning, a way of proceeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Method acting stems from Stanislavsky's system, and a method is also a procedure or course of action.

clue.text: Girl in car, greedy type

indicators.note: in places the girl's name within the abbreviation for the car

parts.note: GT is a gran turismo, a type of sports car
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman in a car turns out to be a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannet is British slang for a greedy eater, from the seabird's voracious appetite for fish.

clue.text: Leader of expedition put down an antelope

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, at the front of the line

parts.note: the opening letter of expedition
to land is to put down, as a plane or a catch

explanation.surface: The head of a safari party shot an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests killing the animal, but it means to land.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: I approach home with sincere intentions

parts.note: taken as written
to near something is to approach it
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone heads homeward meaning every word they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in earnest is to mean it seriously and sincerely.

clue.text: Dig up the earth around small hen house

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the digging word encloses the letter for small

parts.note: to root is to dig in the soil, as a pig does
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone digs over the ground beside a little chicken coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds, especially hens, settle to sleep.

clue.text: Transfer diamonds in German city

indicators.note: in places the card suit inside the name of the city

parts.note: Hanover is a city in northern Germany
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Jewels change hands in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' suggests jewels, but it is the card suit, abbreviated D.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the passing of something, such as power or goods, from one party to another.

clue.text: Muddled situation resulting from other ranks being admitted to service

indicators.note: something admitted to a place is let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Confusion follows when ordinary soldiers are allowed into a military ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests military service, but it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, and figuratively a confused, entangling situation.

clue.text: Set off to make famous college in time

indicators.note: in places the college's name within the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

explanation.surface: Arriving at a famous college punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is England's best-known boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, causing it to explode.

clue.text: Lifted boa — constriction finally follows

indicators.note: follows says this piece comes after the scarf word in the answer

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf, a kind of stole

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of constriction

explanation.surface: A boa snake squeezes its prey after lifting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boa' and 'constriction' conjure the snake, but the boa is a feather scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifted is slang for stolen, as in shoplifting.
